newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to see coffee production deficit - Abecafe.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to see coffee production deficit - Abecafe.

text.p: Brazil is likely to see a production deficit of at least four million 60-kg bags in 1997/98, said the secretary-general of the Brazilian Coffee Exporters' Association (Abecafe).
Abecafe today estimated that the 1997/98 crop would reach 23.2 million bags.
"(Total) demand for Brazilian coffee is of the order of 28 million bags and this is a conservative estimate," said Jose Sette at a press conference.
"We will have a deficit of more than four million bags, nearly five million," he added.
The Brazilian government will have to increase the size and frequency of its stock auctions in order to cover the deficit, Sette said.
"We are going to need regular auctions of government stocks of quite high volume to cover this deficit," he said.
These will have to be distributed equally during the entire year in order to be absorbed by the roasting and export industry, a separate Abecafe statement said.
The sale of four million bags of government stocks in one year would imply an average monthly sale of 330,000 bags.
"One of the ways to diminish the possible negative effect of auctions on prices would be to double the frequency of auctions from one to two per month," Abecafe stated.
